review_messages:
Independent review of MUSIC_CRAFT_PILOT_20261013 (candidate sha256 c1e0dfdf..., editorial sha256 e62aba36... — confirmed matching on-disk frozen files). Reviewer: Claude Sonnet 5, read-only.

BLIND SOLVE (recorded before opening editorial.json): 001=a (Pan), 002=b (move warp marker to beat), 003=c (pop filter), 004=d (sampling). All four match the editorial key.

PER-ITEM VERDICT:
001 Pan — ACCEPT. Fetched ableton.com/en/manual/mixing/ live (HTTP 200, no redirect): verbatim "The Pan control positions the track's output in the stereo field" confirms stem/explanation. audio-fact-sheet/ confirms "constant power panning... signals panned fully left or right will be increased by +3 dB" (editorial says level 'changes' at extremes — accurate, direction not overclaimed). Distractors (tempo/transposition/solo) correctly non-overlapping. No alternate defensible answer.

002 Warp marker — ACCEPT with minor precision note. Both Ableton URLs fetched live (200): audio-clips-tempo-and-warping/ confirms warp markers "lock a specific point in a sample, such as a transient, to a particular place in the timeline." the_fastest_way_to_warp_a_track/ confirms the actual workflow: double-click the transient to create a marker, then right-click > "Set 1.1.1 here" + "Warp From Here." Note: the option text 'Передвинуть warp-маркер к доле' (move the marker to the beat) is a reasonable simplification of this create+snap workflow, but the tutorial doesn't literally describe dragging an existing marker — worth flagging as a terminology simplification, not a factual error. No alternate defensible distractor (solo/return track/overdub don't touch timing).

003 Pop filter — ACCEPT. Shure PGA27 PDF (fetched and text-extracted) verbatim: "Use a pop filter (Shure PS-6) to prevent plosives" and "Reduce plosives... If possible, use a pop filter alone or in combination with the low-frequency reduction setting." HARMAN help page (fetched live after one transient TLS timeout/retry) confirms: "reduce or eliminate popping sounds caused by... fast-moving air... from plosives" and diaphragm-impact mechanism. Shock mount correctly excluded as a distractor (addresses handling/vibration, not airflow). No alternate defensible answer.

004 Sampling — ACCEPT with one concrete sourcing gap. loop-5-perspectives-on-sampling/ confirmed verbatim: "musique concrète – composing by arranging pieces of recorded sound into new musical contexts." However the second cited source, live-manual/11/clip-view/, does NOT contain the phrases 'compressed sample' or 'reference to a sample' or 'sound file' anywhere in its full fetched text (73,535 chars, fully retrieved, no truncation) — I could not find this specific wording on that URL at all. The page does support the weaker/related claim that renaming a clip 'does not rename the referenced sample file,' so the general clip↔sample linkage is confirmed, but editorial.json's sources[1].supported_claim overstates what this specific URL says (attributes a 'compressed sample' definition that isn't there). This doesn't change the correct answer or distractor validity (all four options remain unambiguous, sampling is clearly correct), but the source-claim pairing for that one citation is not verifiable as written.

DUPLICATE/OVERLAP SCREEN (independent, not relying on coverage-notes.md): grepped quizzes/, study/, and quizzes/MusicPeople/*.json (canonical dir, not .run snapshots) for панорам|сэмпл|семпл|warp|поп-фильтр|плозив|шок-маунт|вокал. All 'панорам' hits are unrelated (cat/raccoon panoramic vision, Christmas panoramic-camera trivia, a stop-motion camera-pan distractor in film_craft_20261013.json) — none teach stereo panning. No sampling/warp/pop-filter/plosive hits anywhere. MusicPeople's two existing quizzes are award/credit-recall questions (Carole King credits, Come On Over guest vocalist, Sister Rosetta Tharpe) with zero conceptual overlap with these four craft items. No duplicate found.

OPTION-FORM CHECKS: grammatical parallelism checked per item (consistent noun-case or consistent infinitive-verb-phrase forms within each item); no parenthetical or length outlier reliably flags the correct answer (longest option is correct in only 1 of 4 items, by a small margin).

UNRESOLVED LIMITATIONS: (1) the clip-view source-claim mismatch above is a documentation/citation-accuracy issue, not a correctness issue for the question; (2) I did not re-verify every other quiz file in the repo beyond the targeted lexical grep (same scope limitation coverage-notes.md itself discloses); (3) HARMAN URL required one retry due to a transient TLS handshake timeout before succeeding — noting this as an actual access hiccup, not silently smoothed over.

OVERALL: four items are independently source-supported for their core claims and the correct options are unambiguous; recommend ACCEPT for the draft with one citation-accuracy note on item 004's second source to fix before/at canonical integration (not a blocker for this draft-only review).
